dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Preseptal (periorbital) cellulitis of the right upper eyelid, likely secondary to bacterial spread from a recent ipsilateral upper respiratory/sinus infection (most consistent with ethmoid sinus involvement).

1. Orbital (postseptal) cellulitis - cannot be fully excluded without imaging; would warrant emergent contrast-enhanced CT orbits/sinuses.
2. Lacrimal gland inflammation (acute dacryoadenitis) - could cause localized upper outer-lid swelling and erythema.
3. Early contact/dermal periorbital inflammatory process (e.g., stye/chalazion or insect hypersensitivity reaction) - less likely given the degree of edema and recent URI.
